laws.rule: The legal age for cannabis in Prince Edward Island is 19. Adults may carry up to 30 g of dried cannabis (or equivalent) in public, and buy only from government-operated stores.

Prince Edward Island is stricter than most provinces on where cannabis may be used. Under the Cannabis Control Act, R.S.P.E.I., c. C-1.2, s. 13(1), a person aged 19 or over may only consume cannabis in a private dwelling (as, or with the consent of, the occupant), on vacant land (with the occupant's consent), or in a place set out in regulations. There is no general allowance for public places. Consuming in or on a vehicle on a highway or trail, moving or not, is banned (s. 14(1)), and so is consuming in or on a boat unless the boat is a private dwelling (s. 14(2)). Buying cannabis from anyone other than an authorised vendor is banned (s. 10(1)); gifts are limited to adults 19 and over (s. 11). The consolidation read is current to 1 August 2023.

Nobody may operate a vehicle or boat, or have care and control of one, moving or not, with cannabis in it, unless it is in its unopened purchase package, packed in a fastened-closed container not readily available to anyone in the vehicle or boat, in a vehicle or boat used as a private dwelling, or carried by a bus or taxi passenger (s. 15(1) and (2)). Section 16 states that nothing in the Act authorises smoking cannabis where the Smoke-free Places Act bans smoking.

Liquor Control Act, R.S.P.E.I. 1988, c. L-14, s. 39: nobody may drink liquor in a public place except on licensed premises where it is served, nobody may be intoxicated in a public place, and nobody may drink liquor in or about a motor vehicle. The legal drinking age is 19: it is an offence to sell, give or supply liquor to anyone under or apparently under 19 (s. 40(1)), and for a person under 19 to have or drink liquor, except liquor given by a parent, guardian or spouse for beverage purposes or administered for medical reasons (s. 40(5) and (6)). The consolidation read is current to 22 June 2024.

A person lawfully holding liquor may carry it in a motor vehicle, but if its excise stamp or seal is broken the package must go in the trunk, or in a locked container (not the glove or map compartment) in a part of the vehicle not readily reachable by the driver or passengers (Liquor Control Act, s. 21).

items.text: You must be 19 or older to buy, possess or grow cannabis. The only legal way to buy recreational cannabis is through PEI Cannabis stores. Adults may carry up to 30 g of dried cannabis (or equivalent) in public.

It's illegal to use cannabis in public spaces. Use is allowed in a private dwelling, which includes a home, apartment, hotel room, campsite or condo and an attached balcony or deck, though owners and operators can set their own rules. You can't use cannabis in any vehicle (car, boat, off-road vehicle), moving or not. In a vehicle, keep it in a sealed container out of reach of the driver and passengers.

The legal drinking age is 19. The Liquor Control Act bans drinking in a public place other than licensed premises, being intoxicated in a public place, and drinking in or around a motor vehicle (s. 39).
